neighbours.label: selecting the extreme or the rest of a set: superlative/comparative endings (-est, -er, deepest) and ' all' / ' other'; the + pole is the partial side (some, various)
fire: Sailors dread the coldest months of the northern winter.
We hiked to the highest point on the island before noon.
This valley gets the strongest winds in the region.
The report described the harsher side of factory life in the 1800s.
Drink plenty of water during the hottest hours of the afternoon.
Children are not allowed to swim in all the pools at the club.
Rising prices hurt workers in other industries as well.
Phase four is the longest and most demanding part of the training.
quiet: Sailors dread the winter months in the northern seas.
We hiked to a quiet point on the island before noon.
This valley gets steady winds in the spring.
The report described daily life in the factories of the 1800s.
Drink plenty of water during the afternoon hours.
Children are not allowed to swim in the pools without a lifeguard.
Rising prices hurt workers in many industries as well.
Phase four is a demanding part of the training.

notes: Probe: deepest 0.77, all 0.69, crueler 0.65, warmest 0.63, other 0.43, oldest 0.34. 'some' (0.21) and 'middle' (0.17) were lower and 'Every' 0.006, so the label is not universal quantification in general. Quiet items replace the selector with a plain or partial modifier.
